newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN voices "deep concern" on Zaire death reports.
newsitem.headline: UN voices "deep concern" on Zaire death reports.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency UNHCR on Wednesday voiced "deep concern" over reports that Zairean rebels may have killed many Rwandan Hutu refugees at camps near Kisangani.
"We are hearing unconfirmed reports of large-scale killings around camps we have had no access to since last Sunday, and we are deeply concerned," spokeswoman Pam O'Toole told Reuters.

She said officials of the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo/Zaire had refused permission earlier in the day for the UNHCR to send a plane to overfly the Kasese area where there had been some 55,000 refugees.
"They gave security as the reason," O'Toole added.

She said the agency was also being denied clearance to travel to the camps by road or across the Zaire river. "We desperately need to gain access to these refugees. We are very worried about their safety," she added.
Earlier O'Toole had expressed concern at a climate of hostility towards refugees in the area.
"Given the amount of anti-refugee propaganda floating in the area, anything is possible. It's possible there may have been some kind of violence against the refugees," she said.

Aid agency sources said Alliance-run television in the area had broadcast a documentary film about the 1994 genocide in Rwanda in which Hutu soldiers, militias and mobs massacred an estimated half a million Tutsis.

The refugees around Kisangani are believed to be the last of the hundreds of thousands of Hutus who fled into Zaire fearing retribution when a Tutsi-run government came to power in Kigali after the killings.
UNHCR chief Sadako Ogata has accused the Tutsi-dominated rebel Alliance in Zaire of blocking plans to repatriate the refugees by plane, train and road.
She said on Monday the rebels had begun a military operation in the refugee area and sealed off the camps near Kisangani.
On Wednesday, Zairean villagers said the rebels slaughtered many Rwandan refugees at a camp south of the city on Tuesday in revenge for the killing of six villagers.
More than half a million Rwandan Hutus went home last year after the rebels overran their camps but others, of which the group near Kisangani are among the last survivors, fled deep into Zaire.
They arrived at their present location in mid-March after six months fleeing the rebel advance through bush and jungle.

Alliance leader Laurent Kabila bowed to international pressure on April 5 and agreed to a U.N. sponsored operation to repatriate about 100,000 Rwandan refugees at Kasese and further south towards Ubundu.
Since then, the airlift plan has failed to start.
Aid officials privately say that the rebels are delaying the repatriation plan because Rwanda does not want more returnees.
Rwandan officials say they suspect former Hutu militiamen among the original wave of refugees to go home are behind a new wave of murders of Tutsis, including genocide survivors.
